newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU nat'l currencies could disappear early - EMI head.
newsitem.headline: EU nat'l currencies could disappear early - EMI head.

text.p: European Union (EU) national currencies could disappear earlier than July 2002 to limit the amount of time shopkeepers must display prices in euros and national currencies, European Monetary Institute head Alexandre Lamfalussy said in a newspaper interview published on Monday.
But he said he did not believe governments would be ready to switch fully to euros before the end of 2001.

Although European economic and monetary union (EMU) is due to start in 1999, its main impact initially will be on companies, banks and financial markets. EU governments have said national currencies could remain in circulation for public use until July 2002 at the latest.
Lamfalussy said in an interview with daily Liberation that euro notes and coins should be put into circulation in October 2001 to avoid clashing with the busy Christmas shopping period.

"Moreover, we are looking at whether it would be better to shorten the period of double circulation (of euros and national currencies) which is at the moment, due to last until July 1, 2002," he said. "We are receiving lots of complaints, mainly from shops."
He added, however, that governments needed time to prepare the switch to euros for the payment of civil service salaries, pensions, welfare benefits and taxes.
"I am absolutely convinced that public administrations, with only a few exceptions, will not be able to make this change before the end of 2001," he said.
He also acknowledged there was a risk retailers would take advantage of the switch to euros to round up prices.
"The risk is a real one. But there are no means for authorities to prevent them rounding up the way. It is up to consumer watchdog bodies to ensure that this is not done systematically," he said.
